title: An innovative approach for serial injection in marginal vein and blood collection from auricular artery in New Zealand white Rabbit
author: Baby, Jacob, et al.

steps.title: Prepare rabbits and housing conditions
steps.instruction: Use New Zealand white rabbits (n = 35; male = 12, female = 23) older than 2 months with average weight 2.18 kg. Maintain a 12:12 h light‑dark cycle at 28 °C and 30–70 % relative humidity. House two rabbits of the same sex per standard stainless‑steel cage, clean collection pans daily with water, and provide food and water ad libitum except during the experiment.

steps.title: Gather required materials and equipment
steps.instruction: Collect the following: rabbit restrainer, local anesthetic (EMLA®CREAM, lidocaine 2.5 % & prilocaine 2.5 %), size 11 sterile surgical blades, cotton, 95 % v/v alcohol, BD Neoflon™ 24 GA IV cannula (0.7 mm × 19 mm), BD Neoflon™ 26 GA IV cannula (0.6 mm × 19 mm), surgical adhesive plaster, 5 ml syringes, blood collection tubes, and heparin lock flush solution (Heparin Sodium, Hep‑Flush‑10, 10 U/ml).

steps.title: Apply local anesthetic to ear lobes
steps.instruction: Apply a thin layer of EMLA®CREAM to the dorsal lobes of both the right and left ears and retain for 10 minutes before any manipulation.

steps.title: Prepare marginal vein injection site
steps.instruction: Shave the right ear area with a size 11 sterile surgical blade, wipe the shaved skin with a 95 % alcohol swab, and ensure the marginal vein is visible; if not, give a gentle tap to engorge the vessel.

steps.title: Insert and secure marginal vein cannula
steps.instruction: Insert a BD Neoflon™ 26 GA IV cannula (0.6 mm × 19 mm) with the needle bevel up, parallel to the marginal vein of the right ear. Observe a rush of blood indicating correct placement. Apply gentle finger pressure distal to the catheter to stop flow, withdraw the needle, cap the cannula with a Luer‑lock plug, and secure it with surgical adhesive plaster in a loop form for serial injections.

steps.title: Prepare auricular artery incision
steps.instruction: Make a 2 mm wide incision on the left ear using a size 11 sterile surgical blade, taking care to avoid inadvertent damage to the auricular artery.

steps.title: Insert and secure arterial cannula
steps.instruction: Insert a BD Neoflon™ 24 GA IV cannula (0.7 mm × 19 mm) with the needle bevel up, parallel to the auricular artery through the incision. A rush of blood will appear due to arterial pressure; apply finger pressure to limit flow, cap with a Luer‑lock plug, and secure with surgical adhesive plaster in a loop form.

steps.title: Flush catheters with heparin lock solution
steps.instruction: To maintain patency, flush each cannula with 0.1 ml of heparin lock flush solution (Heparin Sodium, Hep‑Flush‑10, 10 U/ml).

steps.title: Collect serial blood samples
steps.instruction: For each collection, apply finger pressure distal to the arterial cannula, release the Luer‑lock plug, attach a 5 ml syringe, and withdraw blood slowly to avoid artery collapse and hemolysis. Withdraw an initial 3.2 ml, then collect four additional samples of 2.2 ml each at 8‑minute intervals, totaling 12 ml over 35 minutes. If arterial flow diminishes, gently massage the ear lobe to restore flow. After each draw, re‑cap the cannula and, if needed, repeat the 0.1 ml heparin flush to prevent clotting.

steps.title: Estimate procedure cost
steps.instruction: The total estimated cost of the entire procedure is INR 300.
